title: Enterprise Onboarding, Health Checks, QBRs & Escalation Playbook
author: Maya Chen
summary: Consolidated playbook for enterprise onboarding, integration checklist, escalation matrix, known issues & workarounds, and QBR / health check templates. For CSEs, Support, and Customer Engineering during the first 90 days and ongoing account health monitoring.
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard playbook for enterprise onboarding, the escalation process, integration guidance, known issues & workarounds, and the health check / QBR cadence and templates. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Support, Customer Engineering, and Oncall SREs owning enterprise customers.

Scope
- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private deployments and large Hosted customers with committed spend).
- Covers 0–90 day onboarding plus ongoing quarterly health checks and escalation procedures for sev1/sev2 issues.

Goals
- Ensure predictable, secure, and performant onboarding with clear checkpoints.
- Minimize time-to-value for customer integrations.
- Provide a fast, auditable escalation path aligned with SLAs and contract terms.
- Surface operational risk and product regressions via QBRs and health metrics.

Roles & Ownership
- Customer Success (CSE): Primary onboarding owner, coordinates meetings, delivers QBRs.
- Customer Engineering (CE): Integration work, assist with SDKs, deployment templates.
- Support (Tier 1/2): First responder for incidents, triage, and workaround delivery.
- Eng-SRE / Escalation Engineer: Handles platform-level faults, capacity/latency issues, and P0/P1 incident response.
- Account Executive (AE): Commercial escalations and contract discussions.

Onboarding Phases (0–90 days)
1. Pre-kickoff (Contract signed)
   - Deliver welcome kit and customer runbook template.
   - Confirm point-of-contacts (POCs): CSE, CE, Security, Network.
   - Provision accounts: API keys, Console access, Dedicated pool assignment or Private control-plane credentials.

2. Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Agenda: introductions, objectives, success metrics, timeline, security requirements.
   - Deliverables: Integration plan, SSO/KMS requirements, network allow-lists, data residency needs.

3. Integration (Week 1–4)
   - Tasks: SDK integration, authentication, test prompts, baseline evals (quality), load profile validation.
   - Owners: CE implements SDK + sample app; CSE schedules runbook & monitoring dashboards.
   - Acceptance criteria: Test traffic successfully served at baseline qps, end-to-end request traceable in Redwood Console.

4. Validation & Go-live (Week 4–8)
   - Run load and latency tests against Dedicated/Hosted endpoints.
   - Verify KV/prefix caching, batching policies, and token cost targets.
   - Complete security checklist (KMS/HSM, audit logging enabled).

5. Post-Go-live (Week 8–90)
   - Weekly health checks for first 8 weeks (or until stable).
   - Establish QBR cadence (quarterly) and baseline metrics for adoption, cost/unit, error rates.

Integration Checklist (example table)
| Item | Owner | Success Criteria | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| API keys & access | CSE | Keys provisioned, least-privilege role assigned | Hosted: Console invite; Private: control plane credentials
| Network & Proxy | Customer / CE | Allow-lists configured; TLS intercepted checked | For Private: verify VPN & port mapping
| Auth & SSO | Security / CE | SSO tested for Console access | SAML/OIDC config IDP metadata file
| KMS Setup | Customer / Security | Encryption at rest enabled, key rotation plan | HSM integration if required by contract
| Baseline Load Test | CE / SRE | 95th latency < contract SLO, tokens/sec validated | Use load harness in benchmarking repo
| Telemetry & Tracing | CSE / Platform | Traces showing request path and latency breakdown | Ensure trace ID propagated from customer client

Support Process & SLAs
- Support channels: Support portal ticket (preferred), enterprise Slack channel, and emergency phone for P0 customers.
- Severity definitions and response targets:
  - P0 (Platform down / critical customer impact): initial ack <= 15 minutes, dedicated incident bridge within 30 minutes, resolution target 4 hours (varies by contract).
  - P1 (Severe degradation / data loss risk): initial ack <= 1 hour, workaround or mitigation within 4 hours, target resolution 48 hours.
  - P2 (Partial impact / degraded experience): initial ack <= 4 hours, resolution target 5 business days.
  - P3 (Enhancement / non-urgent): SLA per support plan.
- Ticket workflow: Triage -> Assignment (Tier 1 -> Tier 2) -> Escalate to Eng-SRE/Escalation Engineer if no progress within SLA -> Postmortem for P0/P1.

Escalation Matrix (contact & steps)
1. Triage (Support Tier 1)
   - Confirm scope, collect logs (request IDs, traces), attempt standard workarounds.
   - If P0/P1 or unresolved within 30m (P0) / 4h (P1), escalate to Tier 2.
2. Tier 2 (Support / CE)
   - Reproduce with customer, capture full request waveform, review recent deploys and monitoring dashboards.
   - Open an engineering escalation (ENG-ESC) and notify oncall SRE.
3. Eng-SRE / Escalation Engineer
   - Take the incident bridge, run the runbook for the impacted service (e.g., Dedicated Gateway, KV cache).
   - If root cause is a capacity or kernel-level issue, open a P0 incident and notify leadership.

Escalation Contacts (example)
| Role | Contact / Channel | When to use |
| CSE (owner) | cse-<account>@redwood.ai / Slack | Always included on onboarding-related issues |
| Support Tier 2 | support+tier2@redwood.ai / #enterprise-support | For P1/P2 escalations |
| Eng-SRE Oncall | pager: +1-555-0100 / #oncall | P0/P1 incidents requiring infra changes |
| Customer Engineering | ce-team@redwood.ai | Integration bugs or SDK issues |

Known Issues & Workarounds (living list)
- Intermittent 5xx from Dedicated Gateway during autoscaling window
  - Symptom: brief spikes of 502/504 during scale events.
  - Workaround: use regional fallback policy in routing to failover to a compatible model variant for up to 60s.
- Increased token cost after longer context usage
  - Symptom: sudden increase in per-request token counts when clients don't trim prompts.
  - Workaround: enable prefix KV caching and enforce prompt length via SDK middleware; recommend quantization profile QP-3 for cost reduction.
- SSO login failures after IDP certificate rotation
  - Symptom: SAML assertions rejected.
  - Workaround: ask customer to upload new metadata; temporary service account can be used for admin tasks.
- Private deployment: control plane connectivity flapping after network maintenance
  - Symptom: periodic control-plane disconnects, agents reconnecting repeatedly.
  - Workaround: increase keepalive window and apply circuit-breaker policy on the agent; coordinate maintenance window with oncall SRE.

Health Checks & QBR Materials
- Weekly health check checklist (first 8 weeks):
  - Topline metrics: request qps, 95th latency, error rate, average tokens per request, cost/unit delta.
  - Operational indicators: number of retries, cache hit ratio, tail latency > 95th.
  - Security: KMS audit log entries, failed auth attempts.
  - Action items: list open action items with owner and ETA.
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template agenda:
  1) Executive summary (usage, adoption, business value)
  2) Performance & reliability recap (SLOs met/missed, incident summary)
  3) Cost and efficiency (tokens consumed, batch/caching savings)
  4) Roadmap & feature asks (model variants, private features, observability requests)
  5) Open actions and timeline

QBR Metrics to Surface
- Adoption: active endpoints, daily active users, feature adoption rates.
- Reliability: P0/P1 count (quarter), mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to resolve (MTTR).
- Performance: 95th and 99th latency percentiles for typical prompts, tail latency regression alerts.
- Efficiency: tokens per successful response, cache hit ratio, batching utilization.

Templates & Artifacts
- Onboarding runbook template (attach to ticket)
- Integration checklist CSV (downloadable)
- QBR slide template (pptx link)
- Postmortem template for P0/P1 incidents

Operational Playbooks & Runbooks (links)
- Dedicated Gateway scaling playbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite
- Incident bridge runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Private deployment operator checklist: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops

Post-Incident & Learning
- For any P0 or repeat P1 linked to a customer, schedule a 72-hour incident review with Support, CSE, CE, Eng-SRE, and the customer if requested.
- Convert postmortem learnings into runbook updates and add to known-issues list.

Change History

- 2026-12-22: Updated escalation matrix and added QBR metric definitions.

Notes and Next Steps
- Maintain this page as the canonical onboarding + escalation reference for enterprise accounts.
- CSEs: copy the onboarding runbook template into the account-specific Confluence space and tag reviewers.
- Support leadership: ensure escalation contact rotations are kept up-to-date in the related oncall roster.

For questions or feedback on this playbook, contact maya.chen@redwood.ai or file a change request in the customer-success Confluence space.
